summary: Validated backend config/boundary plus live /web browsing and beforeunload behavior on preview. Config and Wisp checks pass; YouTube opens in-frame; TikTok connects but renders degraded error content; live content origin still serves legacy protocol1 shell (updated frame.mjs/sw.js not deployed).

minor.issue: Live content origin still serves legacy shell (protocol1/no requestId handling), not the updated protocol2 artifact in repo.

ui_bugs.issue: TikTok shortcut reaches connected state but in-frame content shows degraded error page ('Something went wrong') and heavy runtime exceptions.

integration_issues.issue: Remote content shell deployment mismatch: production content.desmos.lol frame.mjs/sw.js are older than local updated assets, limiting expected protocol2 lifecycle/error behavior coverage.

beforeunload dialog is reliably emitted on reload/external-nav/close after user activation; dismiss path verified. Accept-close outcome is inconclusive in automation harness (tool ended with page closed setup error after reporting false).

action_items: Deploy updated /workspace/frame.mjs and /browse/sw.js to the service serving content.desmos.lol, then retest protocol2 requestId lifecycle/error paths.

Investigate Scramjet/TikTok runtime incompatibilities shown in console (read-only Symbol.toStringTag mutations, storage/JSON parse failures) and verify whether this is expected third-party anti-proxy behavior vs proxy regression.
Re-verify beforeunload accept-close behavior in a direct Playwright environment (Chromium + Firefox) outside current harness limitation.
If required product behavior is game index availability on content hostname, align middleware rule for /api/games (currently blocked) versus /api/games/{id}/content (allowed).
critical_code_review_comments: content_origin_boundary currently blocks /api/games index on content hostname due startswith('/api/games/') check not matching '/api/games'; verify intended policy.
Legacy shell at content.desmos.lol indicates rollout dependency risk: parent compatibility is present, but new protocol2 safeguards are not active until deployment.

Browser page behavior relies on status=connected from outer shell; actual target usability still depends on third-party script compatibility and should be surfaced as in-frame capability status where possible.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Live preview /web shows Full-page browsing with TikTok/YouTube shortcuts and correct open-in-new-tab attrs (target=_blank, rel=noopener noreferrer). YouTube opens real in-frame page; TikTok opens proxied URL but degrades to 'Something went wrong' with extensive JS runtime warnings/errors in console. beforeunload dialog appears after activation on reload, external navigation, and close dismiss-path. Firefox automation was not executable via direct python due missing playwright package in this container.
rca of the issue: Primary failure is environment rollout mismatch plus third-party proxy compatibility: repository has updated protocol2 shell/service-worker, but content.desmos.lol still serves protocol1 assets, so new lifecycle/error safeguards are not active live. TikTok degradation reproduces with connected transport and proxied target URL present, while console shows Scramjet rewrite/runtime incompatibility traces and site-script failures, indicating target/proxy execution constraints rather than app-shell shortcut/config routing bug.
